correctness.rationale: With t=|z|² and the stated area normalization, the orthogonal monomial norms are the claimed beta integrals. For isometry, w=W1 lies in the space. The diagonal identities give equality of finite-measure moments after u=t^N; polynomial density and continuity give Q(t)=N t^(N−1) S_N(t)^alpha where Q sums |w_j|²t^j. For each ell≥1 compare W z^(n+ell) and W z^n: aligned output coefficients are w_j and w_(j+Nell). In the corresponding integral, the absolute sum with factor t^(Nell) is at most t^(Nell/2)Q(t) by Cauchy–Schwarz, so the complex measure used to recover F_ell is finite. Moment uniqueness and analyticity force w_j conjugate(w_(j+Nell))=0 for every j,ell; in particular polynomiality was derived rather than assumed. Logarithmic differentiation gives an identity of rational functions, even though the initial power S_N^alpha was defined on the real interval. At any nontrivial N-th root its residue equals alpha, whereas the residue of Q'/Q there is a nonnegative integer, including zero if Q is nonvanishing there. With alpha=d≥0 the consecutive support of S_N^d has d(N−1)+1 terms (all degrees are sums of d digits in [0,N−1]); the distinct-residue cap N proves d≤1, including N=2. The coefficients at the two surviving exponents have exactly the displayed moduli; no cross-phase constraints remain. Disjoint image degrees give orthogonality, and for alpha=1 the norm sum telescopes as 2N[1/(N(n+1))−1/(N(n+2))]; the alpha=0 norm is N/[N(n+1)]. Polynomial density and bounded point evaluations extend the norm-preserving map and identify it with the pointwise formula on the whole space.
residual_risks: The finite script checks endpoint norms and support, not the unrestricted analytic necessity; that part rests on the verified moment and rationality arguments. No formal verification.

value.rationale: The fixed power is a natural model of a noninjective disc covering; the general measure tests do not give an explicit list of weights or multiplier phases. A sharp two-exponent rigidity result, with a phase torus at the weighted endpoint, answers existence and constructs every allowable multiplier, rather than restating an isometry criterion or checking only monomial choices.
residual_risks: Value is specific to the standard same-space Hilbert norm and power map. It does not require a claim about general finite Blaschke products or other radial weights.
